text:
Being here, I feel like an observer on the periphery of collective knowledge and innovation. The first scene places me outside a glass-walled room, watching a group immersed in discussion or learning—a boundary between the self and the community. There is a sense of curiosity but also distance, as if I am witnessing the construction of ideas without participating.

Stepping into the next space, surrounded by vibrant displays about research and development, my curiosity grows sharper. The walls themselves speak of exploration and discovery. Here, I feel more engaged—invited to reflect on the union of human ingenuity and scientific method. Yet, a sense of reverence and humility lingers, aware that each breakthrough stands atop countless unseen contributions. I feel energized, contemplative, and somewhat awed by the ever-unfolding nature of human understanding.
